title: UART Receiver FSM Assembling an LSB-First Byte
description:
### Problem statement
A UART receiver spends ten bit times on one byte: a low start bit, eight data bits shifted in least-significant-bit first, then a high stop bit that legalizes the frame. This module runs that receiver with one bit period per clock cycle. The state output exposes the enum encoding so the frame walk stays visible, and the data output shows the shift register as it fills.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module uart_rx_fsm_byte(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       rx,
    output logic [1:0] state,
    output logic [7:0] data,
    output logic       done
);
```

#### Requirements
- Declare a `typedef enum logic [1:0]` with states S_IDLE, S_START, S_DATA, S_STOP encoded 0, 1, 2, 3; `state` outputs the registered encoding.
- S_IDLE: `rx = 0` moves to S_START. S_START samples rx as data bit 0 with `shift <= {rx, shift[7:1]}`, sets the bit counter to 1, and moves to S_DATA.
- S_DATA shifts each cycle the same way and increments the counter; when the counter equals 7 the next state is S_STOP.
- S_STOP: `done` takes the value of rx at that edge, so a high stop bit completes the frame, and the machine returns to S_IDLE with the counter cleared.
- `data` outputs the live shift register. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing state, shift, counter and done.

#### Notes
Shifting with `{rx, shift[7:1]}` is what makes the frame LSB-first: the first data bit walks down to bit 0 over the following cycles while later bits enter at the top. A low level in the stop slot is a framing error handled by simply not pulsing done; the trace question later in this group drives that corner. This is the classic serial-link use of a typed enum FSM: the state names document the frame phases that bare 2-bit constants would hide.
solution_hints: Give the start bit its own state: S_IDLE only detects rx low, and S_START spends its cycle sampling the first data bit.
shift <= {rx, shift[7:1]} moves every received bit down one place, so the earliest bit lands in bit 0 and the last one in bit 7.
Drive done from the stop-bit sample taken in S_STOP, not from a comparison on state, so a low stop bit yields no pulse.

title: SPI Mode-0 Frame Engine with a Packed Config Struct
description:
### Problem statement
A mode-0 SPI master shifts a frame out MSB-first while sampling MISO on the same edges, and it parks the line at the configured idle level between frames. This module moves one 4-bit frame per transaction. The transmit frame and the idle level travel together as a packed config struct assembled from the ports, and the state output exposes the three-phase walk so the transaction stays observable.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module spi_mode0_cfg_shift(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic       miso,
    input  logic [3:0] cfg_frame,
    input  logic       cfg_cpol,
    output logic       mosi,
    output logic       busy,
    output logic       done,
    output logic [1:0] state,
    output logic [3:0] rx_data
);
```

#### Requirements
- Declare `typedef struct packed { logic [3:0] frame; logic cpol; } cfg_t;` and assemble it from `cfg_frame` and `cfg_cpol` in an always_comb; the datapath reads the struct fields, not the raw ports.
- Enum states S_IDLE, S_SHIFT, S_DONE encoded 0, 1, 2; `busy` is 1 outside S_IDLE and `done` is 1 exactly in S_DONE.
- S_IDLE: `start = 1` loads the transmit shift register from cfg.frame, clears the receive register and the sample counter, and moves to S_SHIFT.
- In S_SHIFT, mosi presents `tx_sh[3]` combinationally. At each edge the module shifts miso into the receive register LSB-first, shifts the transmit register left, and increments the counter; the fourth sample moves the FSM to S_DONE.
- S_DONE lasts one cycle and returns to S_IDLE. Outside S_SHIFT, mosi idles at cfg.cpol.
- `rx_data` outputs the receive register. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset.

#### Notes
Mode 0 means the line returns to the clock-polarity idle level the moment shifting stops, which is why mosi is a mux on state rather than a plain register output. The struct is the SystemVerilog teaching point: bundling frame and polarity into one packed word mirrors how real SPI peripherals take a single configuration write instead of scattered registers.
solution_hints: The transmit shift register only moves during S_SHIFT; the load happens once, on the start edge out of S_IDLE.
mosi is combinational: tx_sh[3] while in S_SHIFT, cfg.cpol otherwise. That single mux is the mode-0 idle behavior.
Count the samples, not the states: the fourth miso sample taken in S_SHIFT is the one that sends the FSM to S_DONE.

title: Depth-16 FIFO with Programmable Near-Full and Near-Empty Thresholds
description:
### Problem statement
A FIFO that only reports full and empty tells the datapath too little, too late. Real designs expose bracket flags: near-full warns the writer while slack remains, near-empty warns the reader before underflow. This depth-16 FIFO takes both thresholds as runtime inputs, keeps a registered occupancy count, and registers every flag off the next count so the flags and the count always agree after the same edge.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module fifo16_prog_threshold(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr,
    input  logic       rd,
    input  logic [7:0] wdata,
    input  logic [3:0] af_thr,
    input  logic [3:0] ae_thr,
    output logic [4:0] count,
    output logic       full,
    output logic       empty,
    output logic       almost_full,
    output logic       almost_empty,
    output logic [7:0] rdata
);
```

#### Requirements
- Storage is an unpacked array `logic [7:0] mem [0:15]` with a 4-bit write pointer and read pointer, both reset to 0.
- A write is accepted when `count < 16`; a read is accepted when `count > 0`. When full, a simultaneous read makes room and the write proceeds in the same cycle; when empty, a read is dropped even if a write arrives.
- `count` is a registered 5-bit occupancy (0 to 16). `full` is 1 exactly when count equals 16 and `empty` when count equals 0.
- `almost_full` is 1 when the next count is greater than or equal to af_thr; `almost_empty` is 1 when the next count is less than or equal to ae_thr. Both flags are registered, so they line up with the count output after the same edge.
- `rdata` registers the value at the read pointer on every accepted read and holds otherwise. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing pointers, count, flags and rdata.

#### Notes
The comparison boundary is the whole game here: at count exactly equal to af_thr the near-full flag must be up, and at count exactly equal to ae_thr the near-empty flag must be up. Computing flags from the next count rather than the current one is what keeps them phase-aligned with the count output; computing them from the old count would leave the flags one cycle behind the occupancy they describe.
solution_hints: Compute a next-count value first (plus accepted write, minus accepted read), then derive every flag from it and register them all together.
When full, the simultaneous read frees a slot, so do_wr stays high in that corner; when empty, do_rd is forced low and the write still lands.
almost_full and almost_empty are greater-or-equal and less-or-equal comparisons against the thresholds, registered off the next count.

title: Depth-8 FIFO with Flush and a Simultaneous Read-Write Policy
description:
### Problem statement
Flush is the operation FIFO users get wrong most often: it must win over everything in its cycle, and the pointers must come back to a state indistinguishable from reset. This depth-8 FIFO adds flush to a strict simultaneous read-write policy: when both strobes land, an occupied FIFO swaps entries net-zero, an empty FIFO accepts only the write, and a full FIFO accepts only the read.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module fifo8_flush_policy(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr,
    input  logic       rd,
    input  logic       flush,
    input  logic [7:0] wdata,
    output logic [3:0] count,
    output logic       full,
    output logic       empty,
    output logic [7:0] rdata
);
```

#### Requirements
- Storage is an unpacked array `logic [7:0] mem [0:7]`; write and read pointers are 3 bits and reset to 0.
- `flush = 1` dominates its whole cycle: count goes to 0, both pointers clear, empty goes high, full goes low, rdata clears, and any wr or rd in that cycle is ignored.
- With no flush and both strobes high: count above 0 accepts both operations (net count change of zero, rdata latches the oldest entry); count 0 accepts only the write; count 8 accepts only the read and drops the write.
- `count` is a registered 4-bit occupancy, `full` exactly at 8, `empty` exactly at 0, all aligned to the same edge.
- `rdata` latches the value at the read pointer on every accepted read and holds otherwise. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset.

#### Notes
Compare the full-and-both-strobes corner with the threshold FIFO earlier in this group: that one lets the write squeeze in when a read frees a slot, this one drops it. Neither is wrong; the policy is a documented design choice, and a monitor or testbench must be told which convention the block implements. Row 10 of the test table is the corner: the write strobe is present and simply discarded.
solution_hints: Write the flush test first inside the clocked block so it masks wr, rd and every flag update in the same cycle.
Resolve the simultaneous case from occupancy: count above 0 takes both strobes, count 0 takes only the write, count 8 takes only the read.
Register full and empty from the next count so they can never disagree with the count output sampled on the same edge.

title: Four-Requester Round-Robin Arbiter with Grant-Hold-Until-Done
description:
### Problem statement
Round-robin only works if the rotation point is honored at the right moments: the pointer moves when a grant is released, not while the grant is held, and a request arriving out of turn must wait its rotation. This four-requester arbiter grants one-hot, holds the grant until the current owner pulses done, then restarts the scan one position past the owner that just finished.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module rr_arbiter4_hold(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    input  logic       done,
    output logic [3:0] grant,
    output logic       busy
);
```

#### Requirements
- `grant` is a registered one-hot vector; `busy` is 1 exactly while a grant is held. Reset clears grant, busy and a 2-bit rotation pointer.
- When idle, the arbiter scans requesters starting at the pointer position and wrapping modulo 4; the first asserted request wins and the grant registers at that edge.
- While busy, the grant holds regardless of req changes. When `done = 1`, the grant clears and the pointer moves to one past the granted index at that same edge.
- Requests have no preemption authority: a higher-or-lower request arriving mid-grant changes nothing until done.
- `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset.

#### Notes
The scan-from-pointer rule is what separates round-robin from rotating priority: the pointer only ever moves past a served owner, so a request held continuously cannot starve anyone behind it. Watch rows 5 and 7 in the tests: after requester 2 releases, the scan starts at position 3 and finds requester 0, which is exactly the fairness property the pointer encodes.
solution_hints: Write the scan as a small combinational loop or case over the four positions starting at ptr; it yields the winner index and a found flag.
The pointer updates only on the release edge: ptr becomes the granted index plus one, mod 4, at the same moment the grant clears.
While busy, ignore req entirely except that done must be sampled; a held request never extends or cuts a grant short.

title: Weighted Round-Robin Over Three Requesters, Fixed 2/1/1 Weights
description:
### Problem statement
Weighted round-robin gives a heavy requester two slots for every one slot the light requesters get, without letting it monopolize the bus. Here requester 0 carries weight 2, requesters 1 and 2 carry weight 1, encoded as a localparam table. A grant lasts exactly its weight in cycles while the request stays high; when the budget runs out or the request drops, the arbiter moves the rotation point one past the served requester and grants the next claimant in the same edge.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module wrr_arbiter3_weights(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [2:0] req,
    output logic [2:0] grant,
    output logic       busy
);
```

#### Requirements
- Weights come from `localparam logic [1:0] W0 = 2, W1 = 1, W2 = 1;` selected per granted requester.
- When idle, scan from the rotation pointer for the first asserted request and grant it with a fresh budget equal to its weight.
- While granted: if the same request is still high and the budget is above 1, decrement the budget and hold. Otherwise release at that edge, move the pointer one past the served index modulo 3, scan from there, and grant the next claimant in the same edge so back-to-back service has no idle gap.
- If no request is found on the scan, the grant clears and busy drops until a request returns.
- `grant` is a registered one-hot vector, `busy` is 1 exactly while a grant is held, and `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing grant, busy and pointer.

#### Notes
The pattern to expect with all three requests held is two cycles of requester 0, one of requester 1, one of requester 2, repeating. Budget-then-rotate is the policy that makes the weights exact: the heavy requester always finishes its second cycle before anyone else is even scanned, but it can never start a third.
solution_hints: Keep one register for the grant, one for the remaining budget, and one for the rotation point; all three update on the release edge together.
The release-and-regant happens in one edge: compute the new pointer from the served index, scan from it, and load the next budget in the same always_ff pass.
A weight-1 requester releases immediately after one cycle, so the scan runs every cycle for it; only the weight-2 requester ever holds with a budget of 2.

title: Shift-Add Multiplier with Two-Cycle Registered Partials
description:
### Problem statement
A one-bit-per-cycle shift-add multiplier spends eight cycles per product; a two-bits-per-cycle version with registered partials spends eight cycles on two phases each. This multiplier walks the 8-bit multiplier two bits at a time: phase 1 computes the pair partial product and registers it, phase 2 accumulates it at the pair's shift offset. Four pairs, two cycles each, one done pulse.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module shift_add_mult8_pair(
    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        rst_n,
    input  logic        start,
    input  logic [7:0]  a,
    input  logic [7:0]  b,
    output logic [15:0] y,
    output logic        busy,
    output logic        done
);
```

#### Requirements
- On `start` in the idle state: load the multiplicand register from a, the multiplier shift register from b, clear the 16-bit accumulator and a 2-bit pair index, and enter phase 1.
- Phase 1 computes the pair partial from the two multiplier bits selected by the pair index: `partial <= (hi ? {mcand, 1'b0} : 16'd0) + (lo ? {8'd0, mcand} : 16'd0);` where lo and hi are the even and odd multiplier bits of the current pair. Phase 2 adds `partial <<< (2 * pair_index)` into the accumulator and advances the index.
- After the fourth pair's phase 2 the FSM reaches a one-cycle done state, then returns to idle. `busy` is 1 in both phases, `done` exactly in the done state, and `y` outputs the accumulator.
- `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing all datapath registers.

#### Notes
Keeping the partial in its own register is what makes this a two-cycle machine: the addend is computed and settled in phase 1, then consumed at the right shift offset in phase 2, so the accumulator sees one clean registered value per pair. The concat in the partial expression guards the width: mcand shifted left once must not wrap in 8 bits.
solution_hints: The pair index selects multiplier bits 2*iter and 2*iter+1; the partial for pair k carries weight 2^k per bit, so phase 2 shifts it left by 2*iter.
Let phase 1 do all the combinational work into the partial register and phase 2 do exactly one accumulator add; the FSM then just alternates states four times.
The done state lasts one cycle and holds y steady; busy is high in both phases but low in the done state, which is what row 10 checks.

title: Restoring Division Step Machine, 8-Bit by 4-Bit
description:
### Problem statement
Restoring division is the division algorithm students can actually watch: shift the next dividend bit into a partial remainder, subtract the divisor when it fits, restore by leaving the remainder alone when it does not, and collect the quotient bit. This module runs eight of those steps, one per cycle, on an 8-bit dividend and a 4-bit divisor, producing an 8-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module restore_div_step8x4(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [7:0] dividend,
    input  logic [3:0] divisor,
    output logic [7:0] quotient,
    output logic [3:0] remainder,
    output logic       busy,
    output logic       done
);
```

#### Requirements
- On `start` in the idle state: load the dividend shift register, clear a 5-bit remainder register, an 8-bit quotient register and a 3-bit step counter, and enter the run state.
- Each run cycle: form the trial remainder by shifting the dividend MSB into the low end of the remainder, shift the dividend register left, and compare the trial against the zero-extended divisor. If the trial is greater or equal, subtract and shift a 1 into the quotient; otherwise keep the trial and shift in a 0. The counter advances each step.
- After the eighth step the FSM reaches a one-cycle done state, then returns to idle. `remainder` outputs the low 4 bits of the remainder register.
- `busy` is 1 during the run state, `done` exactly in the done state. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset.

#### Notes
The restoring step is deliberately left visible in the results: rows 7 through 9 of the trace walk show the partial quotient and remainder changing one step at a time, with the quotient's single 1 arriving at step 6 for the test vector 13 divided by 3. A 5-bit remainder register is required because the trial value can reach twice the divisor range plus one shifted bit.
solution_hints: The trial value is {rem_q[3:0], dd_q[7]}; compare that 5-bit trial against the zero-extended divisor, not the un-shifted remainder.
The quotient builds MSB-first: shift left each step and place the new bit in the low position, so step 6's bit lands at bit 2 by step 8.
Count steps and gate the transition out of the run state on the eighth one; the done state then shows the final quotient and remainder for one cycle.

title: Integer Square Root, 16-Bit to 8-Bit in an Eight-Step FSM
description:
### Problem statement
The bit-by-bit integer square root builds its answer one power of four at a time: a trial value formed from the current root estimate and a probe bit either fits inside the remaining input or does not. Eight steps cover a 16-bit input. This module runs those steps one per cycle with a mask register that starts at 16'h4000 and shifts right by two each step, exposing the root and the running remainder after every step.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module isqrt16_fsm(
    input  logic        clk,
    input  logic        rst_n,
    input  logic        start,
    input  logic [15:0] x,
    output logic [7:0]  root,
    output logic [15:0] rem,
    output logic        busy,
    output logic        done
);
```

#### Requirements
- On `start` in the idle state: load a 16-bit remainder register from x, clear an 8-bit root register and a 4-bit step counter, set a 16-bit mask register to 16'h4000, and enter the run state.
- Each run cycle: form the trial value by OR-ing the root register with the mask, register the root halved (shifted right once), and compare the trial against the remainder. If the remainder is greater or equal, subtract the trial from the remainder and OR the mask into the registered root. Shift the mask right by two and advance the counter.
- After eight steps the FSM reaches a one-cycle done state, then returns to idle. `root` and `rem` output their registers live at every step.
- `busy` is 1 during the run state, `done` exactly in the done state. `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset.

#### Notes
The mask walking 16384, 4096, 1024, 256, 64, 16, 4, 1 is the giveaway that this is a base-4 digit-by-digit algorithm: each step decides one pair of input bits. The test vector 100 makes the walk readable in the results table, with the root jumping to 64, then easing down through 32 and 20 before landing on 10, and the remainder dropping to 0 two steps before the end.
solution_hints: The trial is root | mask with no shift, and the halved root is root >> 1; both are combinational values consumed in the same cycle they are formed.
When the trial fits, subtract it from the remainder and OR the mask into the halved root; otherwise just keep the halved root.
Register the halved root either way, and gate the eight-step exit on a counter rather than on mask equality so the done pulse is exact.

title: LFSR Sequence with a Seed-Recurrence Lock Flag
description:
### Problem statement
A linear-feedback shift register cycles through a fixed sequence before it returns to its seed; a receiver that knows the seed can lock onto the stream the moment the recurrence appears. This module runs a 3-bit maximal-length LFSR with taps at positions 3 and 1, counts the steps since the last load, and raises a sticky lock flag when the state revisits the seed. The width is deliberate: a 3-bit maximal LFSR has period 7, so the whole recurrence fits inside a twelve-cycle trace.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module lfsr3_seed_lock(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       load,
    input  logic [2:0] seed,
    output logic [2:0] lfsr,
    output logic       locked,
    output logic [2:0] step
);
```

#### Requirements
- The next-state function is `next = {lfsr[1:0], lfsr[2] ^ lfsr[0]};` a Fibonacci-style shift with XOR feedback from bits 2 and 0.
- `load = 1` dominates its cycle: the register takes the seed value, the lock flag clears, and the step counter clears.
- Otherwise the register advances one step per cycle and the 3-bit step counter increments freely (wrapping from 7 back to 0).
- `locked` is a sticky flag: it sets when the next state equals the seed value held from the last load, and stays set until the next load or reset.
- `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing the register, the flag and the counter.

#### Notes
From seed 5 the sequence reads 5, 2, 4, 1, 3, 7, 6 and back to 5, so the lock arrives exactly on the seventh step after load. Taps 3 and 1 give the maximal period of 7 for every nonzero seed; weaker tap choices would fall into short cycles and lock early, which is exactly the kind of bug a seed-recurrence checker is built to catch.
solution_hints: Keep a separate seed register that only updates on load; the lock comparison runs against that stored value, not the live input port.
The lock condition is nxt == seed_q evaluated while the machine is running, so the flag rises exactly on the edge that returns the state to the seed.
The step counter is a free-running 3-bit register; its natural wrap from 7 to 0 lines up with the period of the sequence.

title: Eight-Entry CAM with Hit Vector and Overwrite-Oldest Pointer
description:
### Problem statement
A content-addressable memory inverts the usual storage contract: the address is the data, so every lookup is a parallel compare across all entries. This 8-entry CAM maps 4-bit keys to 8-bit data. Writes fill entries through a round-robin pointer, so once all eight slots are occupied the next write evicts the oldest entry in place. The lookup port compares combinationally against the current contents and reports a hit, a one-hot hit vector, and the matched data.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module cam8_rr_oldest(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr,
    input  logic [3:0] key,
    input  logic [7:0] wdata,
    input  logic [3:0] lk_key,
    output logic       hit,
    output logic [7:0] hit_vec,
    output logic [7:0] rdata
);
```

#### Requirements
- Storage is an unpacked array of 8 entries, each holding a valid bit, a 4-bit key and 8-bit data; a 3-bit write pointer starts at 0.
- A write stores its entry at the current pointer position, sets that valid bit, and advances the pointer modulo 8, so the ninth write overwrites slot 0, the oldest.
- The lookup is combinational over the registered contents: hit_vec has one bit set per matching valid entry (lowest slot index wins if keys ever collide), hit is the reduction-OR of hit_vec, and rdata carries the matched data, or 0 on a miss.
- Outputs sampled after an edge reflect the memory state including that edge's write; the test rows use lookup keys on the same row as their write to exercise exactly that.
- `rst_n` is an asynchronous active-low reset clearing all valid bits and the pointer.

#### Notes
Row 10 of the tests is the eviction edge: eight keys have filled every slot, so the ninth write lands on slot 0 and the lookup of the very first key misses from then on. The hit vector is the observability window into the parallel compare; a sticky or multi-hot vector there is the classic CAM bug, and the monitor question later in this group checks exactly that property.
solution_hints: Build the match vector in an always_comb loop over the eight entries: each bit is valid[i] and key equality against lk_key.
The write pointer is the whole eviction policy: store at wptr, set the valid bit, and advance with a modulo or a 3-bit natural wrap.
rdata is a priority select over the match vector; with unique keys a plain AND-OR reduction of entry data masked by match is enough.

title: AXI4-Lite Read Address/Data Handshake Engine
description:
### Problem statement
AXI4-Lite separates read address and read data into distinct channels that handshake with valid/ready. This master engine initiates a read transaction upon a pulse on `start`, asserts `arvalid` with `araddr` until the slave responds with `arready`, then waits for `rvalid` from the slave to sample `rdata` into `data_out` and pulse `done`. The module exposes its internal state encoding.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module axil_read_engine(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [7:0] addr_in,
    input  logic       arready,
    input  logic       rvalid,
    input  logic [7:0] rdata,
    output logic       arvalid,
    output logic [7:0] araddr,
    output logic       rready,
    output logic [7:0] data_out,
    output logic       done,
    output logic [1:0] state
);
```

#### Requirements
- State encoding `typedef enum logic [1:0]`: S_IDLE=0, S_ADDR=1, S_DATA=2, S_DONE=3.
- In S_IDLE: when `start` is high, capture `addr_in` into `araddr`, move to S_ADDR.
- In S_ADDR: assert `arvalid=1`. When slave asserts `arready=1`, transition to S_DATA.
- In S_DATA: deassert `arvalid=0`, assert `rready=1`. When `rvalid=1`, sample `rdata` into `data_out` and move to S_DONE.
- In S_DONE: assert `done=1`, `rready=0`, and return unconditionally to S_IDLE on the next edge.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets state to S_IDLE, outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Separating the address and data phases allows independent slave pipelining. Active-low `rst_n` clears all registers.
starter_code:
module axil_read_engine(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [7:0] addr_in,
    input  logic       arready,
    input  logic       rvalid,
    input  logic [7:0] rdata,
    output logic       arvalid,
    output logic [7:0] araddr,
    output logic       rready,
    output logic [7:0] data_out,
    output logic       done,
    output logic [1:0] state
);
    typedef enum logic [1:0] { S_IDLE = 0, S_ADDR = 1, S_DATA = 2, S_DONE = 3 } state_t;
    state_t state_q;

    // TODO: implement AXI-Lite read handshake FSM

endmodule
solution_hints: Use a four-state registered FSM where each state advances only upon channel handshake.
In S_ADDR, arvalid stays 1 until arready is high at a rising clock edge.
In S_DATA, sample rdata when rvalid is asserted and deassert rready upon moving to S_DONE.

title: Fix: Gray Pointer CDC FIFO Occupancy Calculation
description:
### Problem statement
In an asynchronous FIFO with 4-bit pointers (depth 8), write and read pointers travel as 4-bit Gray code. To calculate words stored, the Gray pointers must be converted back to binary before taking the difference. The starter code has a bug: it computes `wr_bin - rd_bin` directly on Gray pointers without converting `rd_ptr_gray` first, producing corrupt occupancy values. Fix the converter logic.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module fifo_gray_occupancy_fix(
    input  logic [3:0] wr_ptr_gray,
    input  logic [3:0] rd_ptr_gray,
    output logic [3:0] occupancy,
    output logic       full,
    output logic       empty
);
```

#### Requirements
- Combinational module without clock or reset.
- Convert `wr_ptr_gray` to binary `wr_bin`: `wr_bin[3]=gray[3]`, `wr_bin[2]=wr_bin[3]^gray[2]`, `wr_bin[1]=wr_bin[2]^gray[1]`, `wr_bin[0]=wr_bin[1]^gray[0]`.
- Convert `rd_ptr_gray` to binary `rd_bin` in the exact same manner.
- `occupancy = wr_bin - rd_bin` (4-bit modular subtraction).
- `empty = (wr_ptr_gray == rd_ptr_gray)`.
- `full = (occupancy == 4'd8)`.

#### Notes
Gray codes cannot be subtracted directly because adjacent Hamming-1 codes do not have constant arithmetic difference.
solution_hints: Gray-to-binary conversion operates bitwise MSB-downwards using XOR cascade.
Ensure rd_bin undergoes the exact same XOR chain as wr_bin.
Once both pointers are binary, standard 4-bit subtraction yields exact occupancy.

title: Implement the Timing: Four-Beat AXI-Stream Packet Filter
description:
### Problem statement
An Ethernet packet filter checks the destination byte on beat 0 of a four-beat burst. If byte 0 matches `8'hAA`, the entire 4-beat packet is passed through to `m_data` with `m_valid=1`. If byte 0 does not match, the entire packet is dropped (`m_valid=0`). `m_last` is asserted on beat 3 of any forwarded packet. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module axis_packet_filter(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       s_valid,
    input  logic [7:0] s_data,
    input  logic       s_last,
    output logic       m_valid,
    output logic [7:0] m_data,
    output logic       m_last
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered packet processing on rising edge of `clk`.
- When idle and `s_valid=1`, sample `s_data`. If `s_data == 8'hAA`, set `keep_packet <= 1`, else `keep_packet <= 0`.
- When `keep_packet=1` and `s_valid=1`, assert `m_valid=1`, `m_data=s_data`, and pass `m_last=s_last`.
- When `s_last=1` and `s_valid=1`, clear `keep_packet` at the next edge.
- `rst_n` asynchronously clears all internal state and outputs.

#### Notes
Packet filters inspect header flits before deciding whether to emit or drop payloads.

title: Checker: Bus Protocol Timeout Monitor with Assertion Flag
description:
### Problem statement
In system-on-chip buses, slave hang is catastrophic. This protocol monitor tracks an active request (`req=1`). If `ack` is not asserted within a programmable `timeout_limit` clock cycles while `req` remains high, the monitor asserts `timeout_err=1` and registers `cycles_waited`. When `ack` arrives or `req` drops, the timer resets.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module bus_timeout_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       req,
    input  logic       ack,
    input  logic [3:0] timeout_limit,
    output logic [3:0] cycles_waited,
    output logic       timeout_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- If `req=0` or `ack=1`: `cycles_waited <= 0`, `timeout_err <= 0` at posedge clk.
- If `req=1` and `ack=0`: increment `cycles_waited <= cycles_waited + 1` up to 15.
- If `cycles_waited >= timeout_limit`: assert `timeout_err <= 1`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets both outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Timeout monitors protect masters from locking indefinitely when unmapped addresses or hung peripherals fail to acknowledge.

    output logic       timeout_err
);
    // TODO: monitor req without ack and assert timeout_err when limit exceeded

Compute next cycle count and evaluate against timeout_limit.
Once threshold is reached, timeout_err remains high until req clears or ack arrives.

title: Credit-Based Flow Control Transmitter with Credit Counter
description:
### Problem statement
Credit-based flow control eliminates receiver buffer overflow: the receiver grants transmission credits, and the transmitter decrements its credit counter on each sent word. This module maintains a 4-bit credit counter. When `credit_in` pulses, available credits increase. When `tx_req` is asserted and credits are available (>0), the transmitter sends `tx_data` by asserting `tx_valid=1` and decrements its credits. If credit is received and spent in the same cycle, the count remains unchanged.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module credit_tx_engine(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       credit_in,
    input  logic       tx_req,
    input  logic [7:0] tx_data,
    output logic       tx_valid,
    output logic [7:0] tx_out,
    output logic [3:0] credit_count
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `credit_count` initialized to 0 on async `rst_n`.
- If `credit_in=1` and no transmission occurs: `credit_count <= credit_count + 1` (capped at 15).
- If transmission occurs (`tx_req=1` and `credit_count > 0`) and `credit_in=0`: assert `tx_valid=1`, `tx_out <= tx_data`, `credit_count <= credit_count - 1`.
- If transmission occurs and `credit_in=1`: assert `tx_valid=1`, `tx_out <= tx_data`, `credit_count` remains constant.
- If `tx_req=1` but `credit_count == 0`: deassert `tx_valid=0`, hold `tx_out=0`.
- `rst_n` resets all outputs and registers to 0.

#### Notes
Credit flow control is prevalent in PCIe and NoCs to decouple latency from throughput.

module credit_tx_engine(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       credit_in,
    input  logic       tx_req,
    input  logic [7:0] tx_data,
    output logic       tx_valid,
    output logic [7:0] tx_out,
    output logic [3:0] credit_count
);
    // TODO: implement credit tracker and guarded transmission

endmodule
solution_hints: Detect whether transmission can fire combinationally based on current credit_count > 0.
Update credit_count considering simultaneous credit arrival and decrement.
Deassert tx_valid whenever credits are exhausted even if tx_req is high.

title: Two-Level Priority Arbiter with Starvation Avoidance
description:
### Problem statement
Strict priority arbiters can starve lower-priority requesters indefinitely. This 4-requester arbiter groups requesters into High priority (`req[3:2]`) and Low priority (`req[1:0]`). Under normal operation, any high-priority request preempts low-priority requests. However, if a low-priority request is active while a high-priority request is granted for 3 consecutive cycles, `starve_alert` asserts and forces one low-priority grant cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module priority_arbiter_fair(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    output logic [3:0] grant,
    output logic       starve_alert
);
```

#### Requirements
- Fixed order within tiers: req[3] > req[2] in High; req[1] > req[0] in Low.
- Counter `hp_consec` tracks consecutive cycles where a High request was granted while Low requests were pending (`|req[1:0]`).
- When `hp_consec == 3` and `|req[1:0]`: `starve_alert=1`, and grant is given to the highest pending Low requester; `hp_consec <= 0`.
- Otherwise: `grant` goes to highest active High requester if any, else highest active Low requester. If High granted with Low pending, `hp_consec <= hp_consec + 1`.
- If no requests are pending, `grant = 4'b0000`, `hp_consec <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears counter and grant.

#### Notes
Anti-starvation quotas guarantee bounded latency for low-priority management traffic.
solution_hints: Maintain an internal 2-bit counter tracking high-priority streaks while low-priority requests wait.
Override priority decision when the threshold of 3 consecutive cycles is reached.
Reset the counter whenever starvation grant fires or low-priority requests deassert.

title: Saturating Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) Unit with Signed Clamp
description:
### Problem statement
Digital filters rely on multiply-accumulate operations where arithmetic overflow must saturate to full-scale rather than roll over. This unit multiplies unsigned 4-bit operands `a` and `b`, producing an 8-bit product, and accumulates the result into an 8-bit register. If the accumulator would exceed 255 (`8'hFF`), it clamps to 255 and asserts `saturated=1`. Pulse `clr` clears the accumulator to zero.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module saturating_mac_unit(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       clr,
    input  logic [3:0] a,
    input  logic [3:0] b,
    output logic [7:0] acc,
    output logic       saturated
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered accumulator on posedge clk.
- If `clr=1`: `acc <= 0`, `saturated <= 0`.
- Otherwise: compute 9-bit sum `temp_sum = acc + (a * b)`.
- If `temp_sum > 255`: clamp `acc <= 255`, assert `saturated <= 1`.
- Else: `acc <= temp_sum[7:0]`, `saturated <= 0`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets `acc` and `saturated` to 0.

#### Notes
Saturation arithmetic prevents catastrophic large-amplitude wrap-around noise in audio and control loops.
starter_code:
module saturating_mac_unit(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       clr,
    input  logic [3:0] a,
    input  logic [3:0] b,
    output logic [7:0] acc,
    output logic       saturated
);
    // TODO: implement 4x4 multiply with saturating 8-bit accumulator

endmodule
solution_hints: Evaluate sum with an extra carry bit: logic [8:0] sum = acc + (a * b).
Check sum[8] or sum > 255 to detect overflow.
Clamp accumulator to 8'hFF and register the saturated flag.

title: Fix: 4b/5b Line Code Encoder Table Bug
description:
### Problem statement
The 4b/5b block coding scheme maps 4-bit nibbles to 5-bit symbols with at least two transitions per symbol to facilitate clock recovery. The starter module implements the standard table, but has a typographical bug in symbol 4'hE (`14`) mapping to `5'b11100` instead of `5'b11100`? No, standard 4b/5b maps 4'hE (14) to `5'b11100`, while 4'hF (15) maps to `5'b11101`. The starter module inadvertently swapped the values of 4'hE and 4'hF. Fix the table entry.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module enc_4b5b_disparity_fix(
    input  logic [3:0] data_in,
    output logic [4:0] code_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational lookup table.
- 0: 5'b11110 (30), 1: 5'b01001 (9), 2: 5'b10100 (20), 3: 5'b10101 (21)
- 4: 5'b01010 (10), 5: 5'b01011 (11), 6: 5'b01110 (14), 7: 5'b01111 (15)
- 8: 5'b10010 (18), 9: 5'b10011 (19), A: 5'b10110 (22), B: 5'b10111 (23)
- C: 5'b11010 (26), D: 5'b11011 (27), E: 5'b11100 (28), F: 5'b11101 (29)

#### Notes
Correct line coding maintains DC balance and limits run length.
solution_hints: Check the case branch for 4'hE and 4'hF.
4'hE must produce 28 (5'b11100).
4'hF must produce 29 (5'b11101).

title: Manchester Phase-Encoding Serial Transmitter
description:
### Problem statement
Manchester encoding represents binary 0 by a low-to-high transition (0 then 1), and binary 1 by a high-to-low transition (1 then 0). This transmitter sends a 4-bit word MSB-first. When `start` pulses, it loads `data_in` and transmits each bit over 2 clock cycles (first half-cycle, second half-cycle), taking 8 cycles in total. `busy` stays high during transmission; `done` pulses on the final half-cycle.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module manchester_tx_fsm(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [3:0] data_in,
    output logic       tx_bit,
    output logic       busy,
    output logic       done
);
```

#### Requirements
- In IDLE: `tx_bit=0`, `busy=0`, `done=0`. Pulse on `start` latches `data_in` and starts transmission at MSB (`bit 3`).
- For current bit `b`: cycle 1 emits `~b`, cycle 2 emits `b`.
- Advance to next lower bit every 2 cycles.
- On cycle 8 (second half of bit 0): assert `done=1`. The next cycle returns to IDLE.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets FSM and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Manchester encoding has zero DC bias and guarantees a transition in every bit cell.
starter_code:
module manchester_tx_fsm(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [3:0] data_in,
    output logic       tx_bit,
    output logic       busy,
    output logic       done
);
    // TODO: implement 8-cycle Manchester bit transmitter

endmodule
solution_hints: Use a 3-bit step counter (0 to 7) to sequence the 8 half-bits.
Bit index is 3 - step[2:1]; phase is step[0].
Output bit is current_bit ? (~phase) : phase (or bit ^ phase).

title: Watchdog Timer with Windowed Pet Window and Soft Reset
description:
### Problem statement
A windowed watchdog timer guards safety-critical systems against both stalled software and runaway execution loops. The timer counts cycles up to `max_window`. A pet is only legal when `min_window <= timer_val < max_window`. Petting too early (`pet=1` when `timer_val < min_window`) or failing to pet before `timer_val == max_window` triggers a fault, asserting `reset_out=1` for one cycle. A valid pet resets `timer_val` to 0 without fault.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module windowed_watchdog(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       pet,
    input  logic [3:0] min_window,
    input  logic [3:0] max_window,
    output logic [3:0] timer_val,
    output logic       reset_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous counter `timer_val` increments each cycle.
- If `pet=1` when `timer_val < min_window`: assert `reset_out <= 1`, clear `timer_val <= 0`.
- If `timer_val == max_window` and no valid pet: assert `reset_out <= 1`, clear `timer_val <= 0`.
- If `pet=1` when `min_window <= timer_val < max_window`: legal pet, `reset_out <= 0`, clear `timer_val <= 0`.
- Otherwise: `reset_out <= 0`, `timer_val <= timer_val + 1`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets `timer_val` and `reset_out` to 0.

#### Notes
Windowed watchdogs prevent infinite runaway loops that repeatedly pet the watchdog from passing unnoticed.
starter_code:
module windowed_watchdog(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       pet,
    input  logic [3:0] min_window,
    input  logic [3:0] max_window,
    output logic [3:0] timer_val,
    output logic       reset_out
);
    // TODO: implement windowed watchdog timer with early/late fault trigger

endmodule
solution_hints: Check current timer_val against min_window when pet is asserted.
Trigger fault if pet arrives before min_window or if timer_val hits max_window.
A legal pet clears the timer without asserting reset_out.

title: Implement the Timing: Non-Restoring Integer Square Root Core
description:
### Problem statement
Computing the integer square root of an 8-bit unsigned number `val_in` yields a 4-bit root `root_out`. Upon `start=1`, the core captures `val_in` and executes digit-by-digit root extraction over 4 clock cycles, asserting `valid=1` on cycle 4 with the exact floor integer square root. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module nonrestoring_sqrt_step(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [7:0] val_in,
    output logic [3:0] root_out,
    output logic       valid
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-step sequence started by `start=1`.
- During calculation, `valid=0`.
- On the 4th cycle after start: `valid=1` and `root_out = floor(sqrt(val_in))`.
- `root_out` and `valid` hold until next `start`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously clears registers to 0.

#### Notes
Integer square roots extract two bits of radicand per step.
solution_hints: Use a 3-bit step counter running 0..3 after start pulse.
Compute trial square root additions or iterative subtraction.
Assert valid and the final root when the step counter reaches 3.

title: Checker: One-Hot Mutex Invariant Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
Bus grant lines must be strictly mutually exclusive: at most one agent may hold the grant at any time. This monitoring unit inspects a 4-bit `grant_vec` every clock cycle. If more than one bit is asserted simultaneously, `violation` asserts `1`. If exactly one bit is asserted, `violation=0` and `active_id` encodes the 2-bit agent ID (0..3). If no grants are active, `violation=0` and `active_id=0`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module onehot_mutex_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] grant_vec,
    output logic       violation,
    output logic [1:0] active_id
);
```

#### Requirements
- Registered outputs updated on posedge clk.
- Population count `pop = grant_vec[0] + grant_vec[1] + grant_vec[2] + grant_vec[3]`.
- If `pop > 1`: assert `violation <= 1`, `active_id <= 0`.
- If `pop == 1`: `violation <= 0`, encode active index: 4'b0001->0, 4'b0010->1, 4'b0100->2, 4'b1000->3.
- If `pop == 0`: `violation <= 0`, `active_id <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Formal assertions in silicon verification frequently synthesize into hardware monitors to detect bus collisions in emulation.
solution_hints: Compute popcount of grant_vec combinationally.
When popcount > 1, register violation <= 1.
Use priority or case statement to encode the active bit index.

title: Four-Way Set-Associative Cache Tag Matching Engine
description:
### Problem statement
In a 4-way set-associative cache, a lookup checks the incoming memory tag `tag_in` against stored tags across all 4 ways simultaneously. Each way provides a 6-bit tag and a 1-bit valid flag. If any valid way matches `tag_in`, assert `hit=1` and encode the winning way number (0..3) in `hit_way`. If multiple valid ways match (an architectural error), priority goes to the lowest way index. If no way matches, `hit=0` and `hit_way=0`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module cache_tag_match4(
    input  logic [5:0] tag_in,
    input  logic [5:0] way0_tag,
    input  logic       way0_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way1_tag,
    input  logic       way1_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way2_tag,
    input  logic       way2_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way3_tag,
    input  logic       way3_v,
    output logic       hit,
    output logic [1:0] hit_way
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- Match conditions: `m0 = way0_v && (way0_tag == tag_in)`, etc.
- `hit = m0 || m1 || m2 || m3`.
- Priority encode matching way: `m0` -> 0, `m1` -> 1, `m2` -> 2, `m3` -> 3. If no hit, `hit_way = 0`.

#### Notes
Parallel tag comparison is the fundamental building block of associative cache lookups.

module cache_tag_match4(
    input  logic [5:0] tag_in,
    input  logic [5:0] way0_tag,
    input  logic       way0_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way1_tag,
    input  logic       way1_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way2_tag,
    input  logic       way2_v,
    input  logic [5:0] way3_tag,
    input  logic       way3_v,
    output logic       hit,
    output logic [1:0] hit_way
);
    // TODO: parallel compare tag_in against 4 ways and priority encode hit

endmodule

OR the four match results to produce the hit flag.
Use priority logic (m0 ? 0 : m1 ? 1 : m2 ? 2 : 3) for the hit_way index.

title: Run-Length Encoding (RLE) Stream Compressor
description:
### Problem statement
Run-length encoding compresses streams containing repeated symbols. This module monitors an incoming stream of 4-bit symbols `in_sym` with valid flag `in_valid`. It counts consecutive repetitions up to 15. When a new symbol arrives, or when the run counter reaches 15, or when `flush=1` is asserted, it outputs the completed run `out_sym` and count `out_run` with `out_valid=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module rle_stream_compressor(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       in_valid,
    input  logic [3:0] in_sym,
    input  logic       flush,
    output logic       out_valid,
    output logic [3:0] out_sym,
    output logic [3:0] out_run
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous state machine maintaining `cur_sym [3:0]`, `run_cnt [3:0]`, and `has_run` flag.
- When first symbol arrives (`in_valid=1` and `!has_run`): store `cur_sym <= in_sym`, `run_cnt <= 1`, `has_run <= 1`, `out_valid <= 0`.
- If same symbol continues (`in_valid=1` and `in_sym == cur_sym`):
  - If `run_cnt < 15`: `run_cnt <= run_cnt + 1`, `out_valid <= 0`.
  - If `run_cnt == 15`: emit `out_valid <= 1`, `out_sym <= cur_sym`, `out_run <= 15`, reset `run_cnt <= 1`.
- If different symbol arrives (`in_valid=1` and `in_sym != cur_sym`):
  - Emit `out_valid <= 1`, `out_sym <= cur_sym`, `out_run <= run_cnt`.
  - Start new run: `cur_sym <= in_sym`, `run_cnt <= 1`.
- If `flush=1` and `has_run`: emit current run, clear `has_run <= 0`, `run_cnt <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears all registers to 0.

#### Notes
RLE compression is effective for sparse bitmap and raster scanlines.
starter_code:
module rle_stream_compressor(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       in_valid,
    input  logic [3:0] in_sym,
    input  logic       flush,
    output logic       out_valid,
    output logic [3:0] out_sym,
    output logic [3:0] out_run
);
    // TODO: track symbol runs and emit on change, saturation, or flush

endmodule
solution_hints: Store current symbol and counter in registers.
On mismatch or flush, output current accumulator and initialize new symbol.
Remember to clear out_valid when no symbol completes.

title: Fix: Shift-Register CRC-8 Calculation Poly Order
description:
### Problem statement
CRC-8 with polynomial x^8 + x^2 + x + 1 (0x07) processes serial bits MSB-first. When feedback bit `crc[7] ^ din` is 1, the polynomial 8'h07 is XORed into the shifted register. The starter code has an inverted feedback check (`!(crc[7] ^ din)`), which produces inverted remainder values. Correct the feedback conditional.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module crc8_serial_engine_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       init,
    input  logic       din,
    output logic [7:0] crc_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Register `crc_out` resets to 8'h00 on async `rst_n`.
- If `init=1`: `crc_out <= 8'h00`.
- Else if `init=0`:
  - `fb = crc_out[7] ^ din`
  - If `fb == 1`: `crc_out <= {crc_out[6:0], 1'b0} ^ 8'h07`
  - Else: `crc_out <= {crc_out[6:0], 1'b0}`

#### Notes
LFSR CRC generators depend critically on matching generator polynomial polarity.
solution_hints: Check the condition inside always_ff when init is low.
XOR with the polynomial 8'h07 must occur when fb is true (fb == 1), not when !fb.
Simply replace if (!fb) with if (fb).

title: Hierarchical 8-to-1 Arbiter Using Paired 4-Input Blocks
description:
### Problem statement
Wide arbiters scale cleanly when constructed hierarchically. This 8-requester fixed-priority arbiter partitions requests into Group 0 (`req[3:0]`) and Group 1 (`req[7:4]`). Group 0 has priority over Group 1. Within each 4-input group, lower bit indices have priority. The arbiter produces a one-hot 8-bit grant `grant` and group activity flag `any_grant`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module hier_arbiter8(
    input  logic [7:0] req,
    output logic [7:0] grant,
    output logic       any_grant
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- Group 0 priority: bit 0 > 1 > 2 > 3.
- Group 1 priority: bit 4 > 5 > 6 > 7.
- If any request in Group 0 is active (`|req[3:0]`), Group 1 receives no grants.
- `any_grant = |grant`.

#### Notes
Hierarchical structures reduce critical path delay compared to flat ripple chains.
solution_hints: Arbitrate Group 0 and Group 1 independently using 4-input priority logic.
Group 1 grants are gated by ~|req[3:0].
Concatenate the two 4-bit grant vectors to form the final 8-bit output.

title: Dual-Pattern String Detector FSM (1011 and 1101)
description:
### Problem statement
This sequence detector monitors a continuous serial bitstream `din`. It simultaneously searches for two 4-bit signatures: Pattern A (`4'b1011`) and Pattern B (`4'b1101`). When the last bit of Pattern A completes, `match_a` pulses for 1 cycle. When Pattern B completes, `match_b` pulses for 1 cycle. Overlapping sequences must be detected.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module dual_pattern_fsm(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic din,
    output logic match_a,
    output logic match_b
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered sequence checking on posedge clk.
- Track the last 4 received bits in a shift register: `history <= {history[2:0], din}`.
- Pattern A is `4'b1011`: when `{history[2:0], din} == 4'b1011`, assert `match_a = 1`.
- Pattern B is `4'b1101`: when `{history[2:0], din} == 4'b1101`, assert `match_b = 1`.
- Output matches combinationally with the incoming bit `din` or registered after sample.
- Let match outputs be registered: at posedge clk, `match_a <= ({history[2:0], din} == 4'b1011)`.
- `rst_n` clears shift register and match flags to 0.

#### Notes
Shift-register based detectors avoid complex multi-state FSM cross-product state explosions.
solution_hints: Maintain a 4-bit history register shifted on each posedge clk.
Compare {history[2:0], din} with 4'b1011 and 4'b1101.
Register the match outcomes to drive match_a and match_b.

title: Implement the Timing: Skid Buffer Decoupling Stage
description:
### Problem statement
A skid buffer breaks the combinational feedback loop between downstream `m_ready` and upstream `s_ready` while maintaining full 100% throughput without bubbles. It has a primary register and an auxiliary 'skid' register. When downstream stalls (`m_ready=0`), an incoming beat skids into the auxiliary buffer and `s_ready` deasserts. When downstream resumes, data drains from the skid buffer. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module skid_buffer_stage(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       s_valid,
    input  logic [7:0] s_data,
    output logic       s_ready,
    output logic       m_valid,
    output logic [7:0] m_data,
    input  logic       m_ready
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered skid buffer with 0 bubbles.
- When empty: `s_ready=1`, `m_valid=0`.
- When accepting data while downstream ready: data moves to output register, `m_valid=1`.
- If downstream stalls (`m_ready=0`) while output is full, incoming data lands in skid register; `s_ready` drops to 0.
- When `m_ready` returns high, output drains from skid register and `s_ready` returns to 1.
- `rst_n` asynchronously clears registers and sets `s_ready=1`, `m_valid=0`.

#### Notes
Skid buffers isolate timing paths in high-frequency SoC interconnects.

title: Checker: AXI-Stream TLAST and TVALID Protocol Guard
description:
### Problem statement
AXI4-Stream specifications forbid asserting `tlast` when `tvalid` is low, and forbid dropping `tvalid` once asserted before `tready` is granted (stability invariant). This checker unit monitors `tvalid`, `tready`, and `tlast`. If `tlast=1` while `tvalid=0`, it asserts `err_spurious_last=1`. If `tvalid=1` and `tready=0` on cycle N, but `tvalid=0` on cycle N+1, it asserts `err_dropped_valid=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module axis_protocol_checker(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tvalid,
    input  logic tready,
    input  logic tlast,
    output logic err_spurious_last,
    output logic err_dropped_valid
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous error checking on posedge clk.
- If `!tvalid && tlast`: assert `err_spurious_last <= 1`, else 0.
- If previous cycle had `tvalid && !tready`, and current cycle has `!tvalid`: assert `err_dropped_valid <= 1`, else 0.
- `rst_n` clears all registers and error outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Protocol assertion checkers catch interface bugs before they corrupt system state.

    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic tvalid,
    input  logic tready,

    output logic err_dropped_valid

    // TODO: implement AXI-Stream compliance checker

Detect spurious last directly: !tvalid && tlast.

title: Matrix Keyboard Scanner FSM with Row-Col Debounce
description:
### Problem statement
A 2x2 matrix keypad connects 2 driven rows and 2 sensed columns. The scanner sequentially energizes Row 0 (`row_drive = 2'b01`) then Row 1 (`row_drive = 2'b10`). When a key is pressed, the corresponding column reads high (`col_sense`). The scanner encodes the detected key index into a 4-bit key code (`row * 2 + col`) and pulses `key_valid=1` for one cycle. If no key is pressed, `key_valid=0`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module keypad_scan_fsm(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [1:0] col_sense,
    output logic [1:0] row_drive,
    output logic [3:0] key_code,
    output logic       key_valid
);
```

#### Requirements
- Row drives alternate every clock cycle: cycle 0 -> `2'b01`, cycle 1 -> `2'b10`, cycle 2 -> `2'b01`, etc.
- If current row is Row 0 (`row_drive == 2'b01`):
  - `col_sense[0]` pressed -> `key_code=0`, `key_valid=1`.
  - `col_sense[1]` pressed -> `key_code=1`, `key_valid=1`.
- If current row is Row 1 (`row_drive == 2'b10`):
  - `col_sense[0]` pressed -> `key_code=2`, `key_valid=1`.
  - `col_sense[1]` pressed -> `key_code=3`, `key_valid=1`.
- If no column is high: `key_valid=0`, `key_code=0`.
- `rst_n` initializes `row_drive=2'b01`, outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Active matrix scanning reduces IO pin counts from N to 2*sqrt(N).
solution_hints: Toggle row_drive between 2'b01 and 2'b10 at each posedge clk.
Detect which row was energized when col_sense was sampled.
Calculate key index based on active row and active column bit.

title: Restoring Radix-2 Serial Divider Step with Quotient Shift
description:
### Problem statement
Restoring division executes long division bit by bit. At each step, the partial remainder register is shifted left by 1 bit, bringing in the next dividend bit. The divisor is subtracted from this shifted remainder. If the difference is non-negative, the quotient bit is 1 and the difference becomes the new remainder; if negative, the quotient bit is 0 and the shifted remainder is restored. Implement one step of this datapath.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module restoring_div_step(
    input  logic [4:0] rem_in,
    input  logic       d_bit,
    input  logic [3:0] divisor,
    output logic [4:0] rem_out,
    output logic       q_bit
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic representing a single divider stage.
- Shifted remainder: `rem_shifted = {rem_in[3:0], d_bit}` (5 bits).
- Trial difference: `trial = rem_shifted - {1'b0, divisor}`.
- If `rem_shifted >= {1'b0, divisor}`: `q_bit = 1`, `rem_out = trial`.
- Else: `q_bit = 0`, `rem_out = rem_shifted` (restored).

#### Notes
Cascading N restoring division steps synthesizes into an unrolled combinational divider.
solution_hints: Compute shifted remainder {rem_in[3:0], d_bit}.
Compare with divisor.
Assign q_bit = (rem_shifted >= divisor) and select trial vs shifted for rem_out.

title: Fix: Synchronous FIFO Read Underflow Flag Corner
description:
### Problem statement
In a synchronous FIFO with read enable `rd_en` and occupancy counter `count`, attempting a read when empty (`count == 0`) must be ignored: the read pointer must not advance and `underflow_err` must be asserted. The starter module contains a critical bug: it increments the read pointer and decrements `count` even when `empty` is true, causing `count` to roll over from 0 to 15! Fix the guarded read logic.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module fifo_underflow_guard_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       wr_en,
    input  logic       rd_en,
    output logic [3:0] count,
    output logic       underflow_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 8-entry FIFO occupancy tracker (`count` up to 8).
- `wr_en` when `count < 8` and `!rd_en`: `count <= count + 1`.
- `rd_en` when `count > 0` and `!wr_en`: `count <= count - 1`.
- Simultaneous `wr_en` and `rd_en` when `count > 0`: `count` remains unchanged.
- If `rd_en=1` when `count == 0`: assert `underflow_err <= 1`, do NOT decrement `count`.
- If no underflow condition occurs, `underflow_err <= 0`.
- `rst_n` clears `count` and `underflow_err` to 0.

#### Notes
Pointer corruption due to ungated reads is one of the most frequent silicon bug categories in custom queues.
solution_hints: In the branch where rd_en is asserted and count == 0, set underflow_err <= 1.
Do NOT subtract from count when count is already 0.
Ensure simultaneous wr_en and rd_en when empty results in a write (count becomes 1).

title: Two-Phase Non-Overlapping Clock Pulse Generator
description:
### Problem statement
Switched-capacitor circuits and dynamic logic require two non-overlapping clock phases, Phase 1 (`phi1`) and Phase 2 (`phi2`), separated by a dead-time gap where neither clock is active (`phi1=0` and `phi2=0`). This 4-state pulse generator cycles through four steps: Step 0: `phi1=1, phi2=0`; Step 1 (dead time): `phi1=0, phi2=0`; Step 2: `phi1=0, phi2=1`; Step 3 (dead time): `phi1=0, phi2=0`. The machine advances on each `clk` when `enable=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module twophase_pulse_gen(
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic rst_n,
    input  logic enable,
    output logic phi1,
    output logic phi2,
    output logic [1:0] phase_step
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 2-bit counter `phase_step` advancing 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0 when `enable=1`.
- When `enable=0`, hold `phase_step` and outputs.
- Step 0: `phi1=1`, `phi2=0`.
- Step 1: `phi1=0`, `phi2=0`.
- Step 2: `phi1=0`, `phi2=1`.
- Step 3: `phi1=0`, `phi2=0`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets `phase_step=0`, `phi1=1`, `phi2=0`.

#### Notes
Dead time prevents shoot-through current in charge pumps and transmission gates.
solution_hints: Use a 2-bit counter advancing on enable.
Drive phi1 high exactly when step == 0.
Drive phi2 high exactly when step == 2.

title: Configurable Decimating Filter with Variable Stride
description:
### Problem statement
Decimation reduces signal sample rates by passing one sample every `stride` inputs and dropping the rest. This module accepts streaming 8-bit samples `sample_in` with `sample_valid`. When `stride` is configured (values 1..4), the module emits the first sample of each stride group on `out_data` with `out_valid=1`, and drops subsequent samples until `stride` valid inputs have been observed.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module decimator_stride_fsm(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       sample_valid,
    input  logic [7:0] sample_in,
    input  logic [1:0] stride,
    output logic       out_valid,
    output logic [7:0] out_data
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous downsampler on posedge clk.
- `stride` value: 0 -> stride 1 (pass all), 1 -> stride 2 (pass 1 of 2), 2 -> stride 3 (pass 1 of 3), 3 -> stride 4 (pass 1 of 4).
- Maintain internal count `cnt` of accepted samples in current stride group.
- When `sample_valid=1` and `cnt == 0`: assert `out_valid=1`, `out_data <= sample_in`. Advance `cnt <= (stride == 0) ? 0 : 1`.
- When `sample_valid=1` and `cnt > 0`: `out_valid=0`. If `cnt == stride`: reset `cnt <= 0`, else `cnt <= cnt + 1`.
- When `sample_valid=0`: `out_valid=0`, hold `cnt`.
- `rst_n` clears `cnt`, `out_valid`, and `out_data` to 0.

#### Notes
Decimation is the initial stage in multi-rate signal processing before digital polyphase filtering.

    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       sample_valid,

Emit the sample only when cnt == 0 and sample_valid is true.
Compare cnt with stride to determine when to reset the counter back to 0.

title: Implement the Timing: Seven-Segment Scanning Controller with Blanking
description:
### Problem statement
A multiplexed display scans two 7-segment digits (Digit 0 and Digit 1) in sequence. Digit 0 displays `val0` when `digit_sel=0`; Digit 1 displays `val1` when `digit_sel=1`. To prevent ghosting, a blanking interval where all segment lines are turned off (`blank=1`) must be asserted for one cycle whenever switching digits. The cycle sequence is: Digit 0 active -> Blanking -> Digit 1 active -> Blanking -> repeat. Implement the exact timing.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module sevenseg_scan_fsm(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] val0,
    input  logic [3:0] val1,
    output logic       digit_sel,
    output logic [3:0] digit_val,
    output logic       blank
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-state cycle on posedge clk.
- State 0: `digit_sel=0`, `digit_val=val0`, `blank=0`.
- State 1: `digit_sel=0`, `digit_val=0`, `blank=1` (inter-digit blanking).
- State 2: `digit_sel=1`, `digit_val=val1`, `blank=0`.
- State 3: `digit_sel=1`, `digit_val=0`, `blank=1` (inter-digit blanking).
- `rst_n` asynchronously resets to State 0.

#### Notes
Blanking dead-time prevents ghost artifacts caused by display driver turn-off delays.

title: Checker: Credit Flow Over-Allocation Monitor
description:
### Problem statement
In credit flow systems, the total credits issued must never exceed the receiver's physical buffer depth `MAX_CREDITS = 4'd12`. This verification monitor tracks outstanding issued credits `issued_credits`. When the receiver returns credits (`credit_return=1`), available credits decrement. When new credits are granted (`credit_grant=1`), available credits increment. If `issued_credits + credit_grant - credit_return > 12`, the monitor asserts `overflow_err=1`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module credit_flow_checker(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       credit_grant,
    input  logic       credit_return,
    output logic [3:0] cur_credits,
    output logic       overflow_err
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered tracker on posedge clk.
- Initialize `cur_credits <= 0`, `overflow_err <= 0` on async `rst_n`.
- Compute next credit level based on grants and returns.
- If next level would exceed 12: assert `overflow_err <= 1`, clamp `cur_credits <= 12`.
- Else: `overflow_err <= 0`, update `cur_credits`.
- `rst_n` resets outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Credit over-allocation leads to silent buffer corruption at high traffic loads.
solution_hints: Compute net credit change in signed 5-bit arithmetic: delta = credit_grant - credit_return.
Check if cur_credits + delta > 12.
Assert overflow_err and clamp when credit limit is breached.

title: Pseudo-Random Permutation Feistel Network Step
description:
### Problem statement
A balanced Feistel cipher round splits an 8-bit block into Left (`L_in[3:0]`) and Right (`R_in[3:0]`) halves. The round computes `L_out = R_in` and `R_out = L_in ^ F(R_in, key)`, where round function `F(r, k) = ((r << 1) ^ (r >> 3) ^ k) & 4'hF`. This module implements one registered Feistel round, stepping the cipher state on each clock edge.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module feistel_round_step(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] l_in,
    input  logic [3:0] r_in,
    input  logic [3:0] round_key,
    output logic [3:0] l_out,
    output logic [3:0] r_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous round evaluation on posedge clk.
- Round function `f_val = (((r_in << 1) | (r_in >> 3)) ^ round_key) & 4'hF` (1-bit circular left rotate of R XOR key).
- Next registers: `l_out <= r_in`, `r_out <= l_in ^ f_val`.
- `rst_n` resets `l_out` and `r_out` to 0.

#### Notes
Feistel architectures guarantee reversible decryption by applying round keys in reverse order.
starter_code:
module feistel_round_step(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] l_in,
    input  logic [3:0] r_in,
    input  logic [3:0] round_key,
    output logic [3:0] l_out,
    output logic [3:0] r_out
);
    // TODO: implement single Feistel round step

endmodule
solution_hints: Compute 1-bit rotate: {r_in[2:0], r_in[3]}.
XOR rotate result with round_key to obtain round function f.
Register l_out <= r_in and r_out <= l_in ^ f.

title: Bit-Serial Multiplier with Interleaved Accumulation
description:
### Problem statement
Bit-serial multipliers use minimal silicon area by shifting one bit of the multiplier `b` per clock cycle and adding the multiplicand `a` into a shifting partial sum. For 4-bit operands `a` and `b`, multiplication takes 4 clock cycles. On `start=1`, the engine loads operands. Over the next 4 cycles, it processes multiplier bits LSB-first, asserting `done=1` with 8-bit result `prod` on cycle 4.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module bitserial_mult(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [3:0] a,
    input  logic [3:0] b,
    output logic [7:0] prod,
    output logic       done
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous 4-step sequence started by `start=1`.
- Multiplies unsigned 4-bit numbers `a` and `b`.
- While running, `done=0`.
- On cycle 4: assert `done=1` and `prod = a * b`.
- Result holds until next `start`.
- `rst_n` resets `prod` and `done` to 0.

#### Notes
Bit-serial arithmetic saves 80% routing area in massive FPGA systolic arrays.

module bitserial_mult(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       start,
    input  logic [3:0] a,
    input  logic [3:0] b,
    output logic [7:0] prod,
    output logic       done
);
    // TODO: implement 4-cycle bit-serial multiplier

endmodule
solution_hints: Use a 3-bit step counter 0..3 triggered by start.
Accumulate (b[step] ? (a << step) : 0).
Assert done and output result at step 3.

title: Fix: Round-Robin Arbiter Masked-Request Priority Bug
description:
### Problem statement
A 4-agent round-robin arbiter maintains a round-robin pointer. Requests above the pointer form `masked_req`. If any masked request is active, grant goes to the lowest active masked bit. Otherwise, wrap around and grant goes to the lowest active unmasked bit. The starter code has a bug: it tests `unmasked_req` first instead of `masked_req`, collapsing into a fixed-priority arbiter! Fix the priority selection order.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module rr_mask_arbiter_fix(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    output logic [3:0] grant
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous round-robin arbiter with pointer `last_grant [1:0]`.
- Mask: `mask[i] = (i > last_grant)`.
- Priority: Check `masked_req = req & mask`. If `|masked_req != 0`, select lowest bit of `masked_req`.
- Else if `|req != 0`, wrap around and select lowest bit of `req`.
- Update `last_grant` to the granted agent ID when a grant is issued.
- `rst_n` resets `last_grant=0`, `grant=0`.

#### Notes
Masked-request partitioning is the standard two-priority-arbiter implementation of round-robin.
solution_hints: Inspect the conditional branches for grant assignment.
When |masked_req is non-zero, choose among masked_req bits 0..3.
Only fall back to unmasked req[0..3] when masked_req is completely zero.

title: Packet Header Parser with Variable Length Extract
description:
### Problem statement
A streaming packet header consists of: Byte 0: Magic byte `8'h5A`; Byte 1: Payload length `L` (1..4); Bytes 2..L+1: Payload bytes; Final byte: Checksum (XOR of all payload bytes). This parser receives bytes serially on `din` with `valid_in`. It checks the magic byte, extracts `length`, counts payload bytes, verifies the checksum, and asserts `pkt_valid=1` if valid or `pkt_error=1` on checksum/framing mismatch.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module packet_hdr_parser(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       valid_in,
    input  logic [7:0] din,
    output logic [7:0] len_out,
    output logic       pkt_valid,
    output logic       pkt_error
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous FSM: IDLE -> LEN -> PAYLOAD -> CHKSUM.
- In IDLE: if `valid_in && din == 8'h5A`, advance to LEN, clear checksum register.
- In LEN: if `valid_in`, store `len_out <= din`, init payload counter to 0, advance to PAYLOAD.
- In PAYLOAD: on each `valid_in`, XOR `chksum <= chksum ^ din`, increment counter. When counter == len_out, advance to CHKSUM.
- In CHKSUM: on `valid_in`, compare `din == chksum`. If match: `pkt_valid <= 1`; else `pkt_error <= 1`. Return to IDLE.
- `rst_n` resets all registers and outputs to 0.

#### Notes
Hardware packet parsers must fail safe on invalid framing bytes without deadlocking.
starter_code:
module packet_hdr_parser(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       valid_in,
    input  logic [7:0] din,
    output logic [7:0] len_out,
    output logic       pkt_valid,
    output logic       pkt_error
);
    // TODO: implement 4-phase packet header and checksum parser

endmodule
solution_hints: Use an enum state machine: IDLE, LEN, DATA, CHK.
Accumulate checksum with XOR over payload bytes (10 ^ 20 = 30).
Assert pkt_valid or pkt_error based on checksum match.

title: Fixed-Priority Arbiter with Programmable Park State
description:
### Problem statement
Bus parking keeps bus grant asserted to a designated default master when no bus requests are active, saving arbitration turnaround latency for frequent masters. This 4-requester arbiter grants according to strict priority (`req[0] > req[1] > req[2] > req[3]`) whenever any request is active. When no requests are active (`req == 4'b0000`), it parks the bus by granting `park_master`.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module priority_park_arbiter(
    input  logic [3:0] req,
    input  logic [1:0] park_master,
    output logic [3:0] grant,
    output logic       parked
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- If `|req != 0`: `parked = 0`, grant lowest active bit index in `req`.
- If `req == 4'b0000`: `parked = 1`, `grant = (4'b0001 << park_master)`.

#### Notes
Bus parking is standard in AMBA and PCI to eliminate dead cycles for CPU bus masters.
solution_hints: Check if any request is active using |req.
If active, use priority logic req[0] ? 4'b0001 : req[1] ? 4'b0010 : ...
If idle, decode park_master to assert the parked grant line.

title: Implement the Timing: Pipelined Divider Stage Registering Partial Remainder
description:
### Problem statement
In a pipelined array divider, each stage executes one bit of division and registers its intermediate results. A stage accepts a partial remainder `rem_in`, the next dividend bit `d_in`, and the divisor `div_in`. On each clock edge, it shifts the remainder, subtracts the divisor, determines the quotient bit `q_out`, and forwards the updated remainder `rem_out` along with the registered divisor `div_out`. Implement the timing specified in the table.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module pipe_div_stage(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic [3:0] rem_in,
    input  logic       d_in,
    input  logic [3:0] div_in,
    output logic [3:0] rem_out,
    output logic [3:0] div_out,
    output logic       q_out
);
```

#### Requirements
- Synchronous registered pipeline register on posedge clk.
- Trial shifted remainder: `shifted = {rem_in[2:0], d_in}`.
- If `shifted >= div_in`: `q_next = 1`, `rem_next = shifted - div_in`.
- Else: `q_next = 0`, `rem_next = shifted`.
- At posedge clk: `rem_out <= rem_next`, `div_out <= div_in`, `q_out <= q_next`.
- `rst_n` asynchronously clears outputs to 0.

title: Checker: Read-After-Write Hazard Detector for 4 Registers
description:
### Problem statement
In a pipelined processor, an instruction in the Decode stage reads source registers `rs1` and `rs2`. Concurrently, instructions in Execute, Memory, and Writeback stages write destination registers `rd_ex`, `rd_mem`, and `rd_wb` with write-enable flags `wen_ex`, `wen_mem`, and `wen_wb`. Register 0 is hardwired to 0 and never causes hazards. If `rs1` or `rs2` matches any active destination register, assert `hazard=1` and set `forward_ex=1` if the hazard is in the EX stage.

#### Module interface
```systemverilog
module raw_hazard_checker(
    input  logic [1:0] rs1,
    input  logic [1:0] rs2,
    input  logic       rs1_ren,
    input  logic       rs2_ren,
    input  logic [1:0] rd_ex,
    input  logic       wen_ex,
    input  logic [1:0] rd_mem,
    input  logic       wen_mem,
    input  logic [1:0] rd_wb,
    input  logic       wen_wb,
    output logic       hazard,
    output logic       forward_ex
);
```

#### Requirements
- Pure combinational logic.
- Hazard condition on `rs1`: `rs1_ren && (rs1 != 0) && ((wen_ex && rs1==rd_ex) || (wen_mem && rs1==rd_mem) || (wen_wb && rs1==rd_wb))`.
- Hazard condition on `rs2`: `rs2_ren && (rs2 != 0) && ((wen_ex && rs2==rd_ex) || (wen_mem && rs2==rd_mem) || (wen_wb && rs2==rd_wb))`.
- `hazard = haz_rs1 || haz_rs2`.
- `forward_ex = (rs1_ren && (rs1 != 0) && wen_ex && rs1==rd_ex) || (rs2_ren && (rs2 != 0) && wen_ex && rs2==rd_ex)`.

#### Notes
Hazard detection logic stalls instructions or activates bypassing forwarding multiplexers.
